failures.name: Drain line clogged
cause_chain: Dust and algae build up inside the drain line
Water drips from the indoor unit
failures.test: Pour a cup of water into the drain pan.
failures.expected: Water does not drain away within 10 seconds.
fix: Switch off the AC at the isolator.
Place a towel under the indoor unit.
Disconnect the drain hose at the outlet.
Flush the drain line with a wet-vac or water pump.
Pour water in the pan and check it drains freely.
Reconnect the hose, power on and watch for drips.

failures.name: Drain pan dirty or blocked with algae
cause_chain: Slime and algae grow in the drain pan
failures.test: Remove the front cover and look into the drain pan.
failures.expected: Standing water or slime in the pan.
fix: Switch off the AC at the isolator.
Remove the front cover and filter.
Soak up standing water from the pan.
Clean the pan with mild detergent and a soft brush.
Clear the pan outlet, refit the cover and test.

failures.name: Drain hose kinked or outlet blocked
cause_chain: Drain hose is bent, crushed or its end is under water
failures.test: Follow the drain hose to its outlet.
failures.expected: A bend, crush, upward slope or blocked end.
fix: Switch off the AC.
Straighten the hose so it slopes continuously downward.
Clear the hose end so it is not under water or blocked.
Power on and check water flows out.

failures.name: Indoor unit not installed level
cause_chain: Indoor unit tilts away from the drain side
Water collects at the wrong end of the pan
It spills over the pan edge
failures.test: Put a spirit level (or phone level app) on top of the unit.
failures.expected: The unit tilts away from the drain outlet side.
fix: Switch off the AC.
Loosen the mounting plate screws.
Re-level the unit with a slight tilt toward the drain side.
Tighten the screws and test with water in the pan.
failures.safety: Work at height: use a stable ladder.

failures.name: Air filter clogged
cause_chain: Coil gets too cold and can freeze
Weak, poor cooling (and melt water may drip)
failures.test: Open the front cover and hold the filter up to a light.
failures.expected: You can barely see light through the filter.
fix: Switch off the AC.
Open the front cover and slide out the filters.
Vacuum or rinse the filters with lukewarm water.
Let them dry completely in the shade.
Refit the filters and power on.

failures.name: Evaporator coil dirty
cause_chain: Dust and mold coat the coil fins
failures.test: With the cover open, shine a torch on the coil fins.
failures.expected: Fins are grey, black or matted with dust.
fix: Switch off the AC at the isolator.
Cover the PCB area with plastic.
Spray no-rinse coil cleaner on the fins.
Gently comb bent fins straight.
Let it dry 15 minutes, then power on.
failures.safety: Keep water and cleaner away from the control board.

failures.name: Low refrigerant (leak)
cause_chain: Refrigerant leaks from a joint or coil
Coil freezes and cooling capacity falls
failures.test: Look for oily stains on pipe joints and listen for hissing.
failures.expected: Oily residue at a joint or a hissing sound.
fix: Switch off the AC.
STOP: refrigerant work needs a certified technician with gauges and leak detector.
failures.safety: Refrigerant handling requires certification. Do not open the refrigerant circuit.

failures.name: Blower fan motor failing
cause_chain: Fan motor bearings or windings wear out
failures.test: Set the fan to high and look at the blower through the outlet.
failures.expected: Blower turns slowly, stops, or hums without turning.
fix: Switch off the AC at the isolator.
STOP: motor replacement needs a qualified technician and the correct part number.
failures.safety: Electrical part: isolate power before touching.

failures.name: Blower fan obstructed or touching housing
cause_chain: Debris or a shifted blower touches the housing
failures.test: Switch off, then turn the blower slowly by hand with a stick.
failures.expected: It catches, scrapes or something is lodged inside.
fix: Switch off the AC at the isolator.
Remove debris from the blower area.
Re-seat the blower so it does not touch the housing.
Power on and listen.
failures.safety: Never put fingers in the blower while powered.

failures.name: Louver (swing) motor faulty
cause_chain: Swing motor or its linkage fails
Air blows in one direction only
failures.test: Press the swing button on the remote.
failures.expected: The louver does not move at all.
fix: Switch off the AC.
Check the louver is not blocked or jammed.
If free but still stuck, the swing motor needs replacement by a technician.

failures.name: Control board (PCB) fault
cause_chain: Power surge or moisture damages the control board
Unit fails to start or shows errors
failures.test: Check the breaker is on, then read the error code on the display.
failures.expected: Breaker on, but the unit is dead or shows a board error code.
fix: Switch off the AC at the breaker.
STOP: control board diagnosis needs a qualified technician.
failures.safety: High voltage on the board. Do not touch while powered.

failures.name: Temperature sensor fault
cause_chain: Room or coil sensor drifts or disconnects
Unit stops cooling early or shows an error
failures.test: Read the error code and look it up in the unit manual.
fix: Switch off the AC.
Check the sensor plug on the board is seated.
If the error stays, a technician should replace the sensor.
failures.safety: Isolate power before opening the board cover.

failures.name: Front cover or panel loose
cause_chain: Clips or screws on the front cover loosen
failures.test: Press gently on the front cover while the unit runs.
failures.expected: The rattle stops when you press.
fix: Switch off the AC.
Re-seat the front cover clips.
Tighten any loose screws.
Power on and listen.

test_minutes_note: Rough time for each test, estimated by the Ustad team (not from the sources); used to order checks.
